title: Tripper Conveyor
model_title: Travelling Tripper on a Bunker-Feed Belt Conveyor

introduction.definition: A tripper is a travelling car that runs on rails along a belt conveyor. The belt is led up over the tripper's head pulley and back down around a snub pulley, so the material discharges into a chute on the car. By moving the tripper along the conveyor, one belt can fill a long row of bunkers, silos or a stockpile.
applications: Filling coal bunkers in power plants
Silo/bin filling in cement and mineral plants
key_points: Belt forms an S-loop through the tripper
Discharges at any point along the conveyor
Belt must have slack/take-up to allow the loop
introduction.summary: A tripper is a travelling car on a belt conveyor that lifts the belt over a pulley and discharges material through a chute to either side. Moving the tripper along the rails lets one conveyor fill a row of bunkers or silos.

foundation: Support the conveyor stringers and drive frames on steelwork or plinths designed for belt tension, material load and drive torque.
alignment: Survey the structure so all pulleys and idlers are square to the centre line; train the belt empty, then loaded.
piping: Chutes designed for the material trajectory to centre-load the belt; skirts and dust seals at loading points; belt cleaners and plough at the discharge.
commissioning: Check pull-wire emergency stops, belt-drift and speed switches; run empty and loaded; record take-up position and motor current.

routine.task: Check chute flow and belt tracking at the tripper.

periodic.task: Check rails, wheels and travel limit switches.

lubrication: Gearboxes: oil to grade and change interval; open gears and slew bearing: grease to schedule.
Wheels and pulley bearings: grease to schedule.

remedies: Level probes; chute design; clear safely

safety: Guard pulleys and nip points; pull-wire stops along the gallery; bunker grating to prevent falls.

video_tutorials.title: Tripper Conveyor — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Tripper Conveyor.
A tripper is a travelling car that runs on rails along a belt conveyor.
The belt is led up over the tripper's head pulley and back down around a snub pulley, so the material discharges into a chute on the car.
By moving the tripper along the conveyor, one belt can fill a long row of bunkers, silos or a stockpile.
Typical applications include filling coal bunkers in power plants; silo/bin filling in cement and mineral plants; stockpile building on yard conveyors.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Tripper Conveyor works.
Material travels along the belt conveyor.
The belt climbs the tripper ramp to the head pulley.
Material discharges into the tripper chute, which drops it into the bunker below.
The tripper travels on its rails to fill the next bunker.

video_tutorials.title: Tripper Conveyor — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Tripper Conveyor.
Check chute flow and belt tracking at the tripper.
Check rails, wheels and travel limit switches.
Replace pulley lagging and bearings.
Watch for belt mistracking at tripper: spillage, edge damage. Common cause: pulley misalignment, build-up.
Watch for chute blockage: overflow, motor trips. Common cause: wet material, full bunker.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
